\section*{Question 3}

A particle moves along the \(y\)-axis so that its velocity \(v\) at time \(t \geq 0\) is given by \(v(t)=1-\tan ^{-1}\left(e^{t}\right)\). At time \(t=0\), the particle is at \(y=-1\). (Note: \(\tan ^{-1} x=\arctan x\) )
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the acceleration of the particle at time \(t=2\).
\item[(b)] Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at time \(t=2\) ? Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(c)] Find the time \(t \geq 0\) at which the particle reaches its highest point. Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] Find the position of the particle at time \(t=2\). Is the particle moving toward the origin or away from the origin at time \(t=2\) ? Justify your answer.
\item[(a)] \(a(2)=v^{\prime}(2)=-0.132\) or -0.133
\item[(b)] \(v(2)=-0.436\)
Speed is increasing since \(a(2)<0\) and \(v(2)<0\).
\item[(c)] \(\quad v(t)=0\) when \(\tan ^{-1}\left(e^{t}\right)=1\)
\(t=\ln (\tan (1))=0.443\) is the only critical value for \(y\).
\(v(t)>0\) for \(0<t<\ln (\tan (1))\)
\(v(t)<0\) for \(t>\ln (\tan (1))\)
\(y(t)\) has an absolute maximum at \(t=0.443\).
\item[(d)] \(y(2)=-1+\int_{0}^{2} v(t) d t=-1.360\) or -1.361
The particle is moving away from the origin since \(v(2)<0\) and \(y(2)<0\).
\end{itemize}

1 : answer

1 : answer with reason

3 : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : sets } v(t)=0 \\ 1: \text { identifies } t=0.443 \text { as a candidate } \\ 1: \text { justifies absolute maximum }\end{array}\right.\)
\(4:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \int_{0}^{2} v(t) d t \\ 1: \text { handles initial condition } \\ 1: \text { value of } y(2) \\ 1: \text { answer with reason }\end{array}\right.\)
